Looks like sleepin', but the body's

with no will to heal, even the strongest
spell don't do much, they say.{0c:2b2223080001fe}

strings.jp:
{1c:10}神の御子アノイアが
太陽の神『ゼメン』と
太陰の神『ゼウェアク』の
二至高神の啓示を受け、{1a}十三聖者と共に神の教えを人々に説き、
悪魔に操られた友の手によって
その命を落とされてから
すでに5千年もの歳月が流れました。{1a}アノイア教は世界の9割を越す人々に
信仰される大宗教となりましたが、{1a}教会と教皇庁の繁栄とは裏腹に
一部の聖職者の心の病は、
ますますひどくなっているように
思えます。{1a}司祭である私が言うべき事では
ないかもしれませんが、{1a}たとえ信仰心はなくとも
人には本来、他人を愛する心、
他人に感謝する心、そして
人を思いやる心があるはずです。{1a}自分の心を信じ、
他人の心を信じてください。
私も{10}さんを
信じています。{0c:02fb01}

strings.en:
{1c:10}Anoia, the Child of God, received the
revelation of the Two Supreme Gods,
'Zemen', god of the sun, and 'Zeweak',
god of the moon,{1a}preached God's teachings to the people
with the Thirteen Saints, and met death
at the hands of a friend controlled by a
devil. Fully five thousand years have{1a}passed since then.{1a}The Anoian faith has become a great
religion, followed by more than nine in ten
people in the world,{1a}but in contrast to the prosperity of the
Church and the Holy See, the sickness in
the hearts of some clergy seems to
grow ever worse.{1a}It may not be my place as a priest to
say so,{1a}but even without faith, people should by
nature have hearts that love others,
that give thanks to others, and that
care for others.{1a}Trust in your own heart, and trust in
the hearts of others. I believe in you as
well, {10}-san.{0c:02fb01}
strings.tl: Anoia, the Child of God, received the revelation of the Two Supreme Gods, 'Zemen', god of the sun, and 'Zeweak', god of the moon, // preached God's teachings to the people with the Thirteen Saints, and met death at the hands of a friend controlled by a devil. Fully five thousand years have passed since then. // The Anoian faith has become a great religion, followed by more than nine in ten people in the world, // but in contrast to the prosperity of the Church and the Holy See, the sickness in the hearts of some clergy seems to grow ever worse. // It may not be my place as a priest to say so, // but even without faith, people should by nature have hearts that love others, that give thanks to others, and that care for others. // Trust in your own heart, and trust in the hearts of others. I believe in you as well, [HERO]-san.

strings.jp:
{1c:10}この教会は、アノイア暦5060年
アスラ・ファエルが発見された時に、{1a}二大国に強制的に連れてこられた
大勢の発掘労働者の方々が
故郷の家族を思いながら
つくった教会だそうです。{1a}私がこの町に来た時は
司祭も礼拝される方もいない
無人の教会だったのですが
5年前からは私が管理しています。{1a}大勢の人達が、この町で、
そして地下遺跡で
かけがえのない命を落とされました。{1a}ここでその方々の霊を弔い、
今ここで戦っている人達の
無事を祈ることが、
私の使命であると思っています。{0c:02fa01}

strings.en:
{1c:10}This church, I am told, was built in the
Anoian year 5060, when Asla Fael was
discovered,{1a}by the many excavation laborers the two
great powers brought here by force, as
they thought of their families back
home.{1a}When I came to this town it was an
empty church, with neither priest nor
worshippers, but for the past five years
I have been looking after it.{1a}So many people have lost their
irreplaceable lives in this town and in the
underground ruins.{1a}To mourn their spirits here, and to pray
for the safety of those fighting here
now... that, I believe, is my calling.{0c:02fa01}
strings.tl: This church, I am told, was built in the Anoian year 5060, when Asla Fael was discovered, // by the many excavation laborers the two great powers brought here by force, as they thought of their families back home. // When I came to this town it was an empty church, with neither priest nor worshippers, but for the past five years I have been looking after it. // So many people have lost their irreplaceable lives in this town and in the underground ruins. // To mourn their spirits here, and to pray for the safety of those fighting here now... that, I believe, is my calling.

strings.jp:
{1c:10}『魔法具』と『魔法操具』という
不思議な道具を使用する
太陽帝国の医療技術です。{1a}魔法の仕組みについては
私も詳しくは知らないのですが、{1a}唱えた方の精神力を吸い取り、
変質・増幅させ、
相手の方に与える道具であると、
クムランさんに教わりました。{1a}危険な地下遺跡の冒険において
欠かせない魔法ですが、
あくまで、その人の生命力・
自然治癒力に手を貸すだけで、{1a}人の生死まではコントロール出来ない
ことを覚えておいてください。{1a}教会の人間しか唱えることの出来ない
魔法と思っている方も多いですが、
教皇庁が聖職者以外の
治癒の魔法操具の所有を禁止したため{1a}外ではそういった誤解が
生まれているようです。{1a}ですが、治癒の術に必要なものは
聖職者かどうかではなく、
相手のことを一心に思う気持ちだと
いうことを忘れないで下さい。{0c:02f901}

strings.en:
{1c:10}It is a medical art of the Sun Empire
that uses the strange implements called
'Magic Tools' and 'Spell Devices'.{1a}I do not know the workings of magic in
any detail myself,{1a}but Qumran-san taught me that these
tools draw out the caster's mental
strength, transform and amplify it, and
give it to the other person.{1a}This magic is indispensable on dangerous
adventures in the underground ruins, but
it only lends a hand to a person's vitality
and natural healing power,{1a}so please remember that it cannot
control life and death.{1a}Many believe this magic can be cast only
by people of the Church, but the Holy
See has forbidden anyone but the clergy
to own a healing Spell Device,{1a}and that seems to have given rise to
the misconception out in the world.{1a}However, what the art of healing
requires is not being clergy, but a
wholehearted concern for the other
person. Please do not forget that.{0c:02f901}
strings.tl: It is a medical art of the Sun Empire that uses the strange implements called 'Magic Tools' and 'Spell Devices'. // I do not know the workings of magic in any detail myself, // but Qumran-san taught me that these tools draw out the caster's mental strength, transform and amplify it, and give it to the other person. // This magic is indispensable on dangerous adventures in the underground ruins, but it only lends a hand to a person's vitality and natural healing power, // so please remember that it cannot control life and death. // Many believe this magic can be cast only by people of the Church, but the Holy See has forbidden anyone but the clergy to own a healing Spell Device, // and that seems to have given rise to the misconception out in the world. // However, what the art of healing requires is not being clergy, but a wholehearted concern for the other person. Please do not forget that.

何を話していいのか
わかりません・・・{1a}それに、私のことなんて聞いても
面白くないですよ。{0c:02f801}

strings.jp:
{1c:10}では、この名前の元となった、
聖書の中に登場する煉獄の
お話をします。{1a}煉獄を、地獄の1つと
誤解されている方も多いですが、{1a}聖書中に登場する煉獄は、
天界と地獄の間にあり、
死者の霊魂が天界にはいる前に
火によって罪を浄化される場所です。{1a}現在のアノイア教の教義では、
神への強い信仰を持つ者は天界に、{1a}大罪を犯した者、神への信仰を
持たない者は地獄に堕とされます。{1a}そして、信仰をもちながらも、
その信仰が不十分な者、小罪の汚れの
ある者は、地獄には入りませんが、
天界に入ることも許されません。{1a}そのような霊魂は、
煉獄の炎に焼かれる苦しみによって
罪の汚れを清められ
天界に入ることが許されます。{1a}天界と地獄の中間地点、
罪を浄化する場所・・・
簡単に説明すると
こうなるでしょうか。{1a}地獄に堕ちた魂は、
永遠にそこを出ることは出来ませんが
煉獄からは出ることが出来る・・・
それが1番の差ではないでしょうか。{0c:02f701}

strings.en:
{1c:10}Then I will tell you the story of
Purgatory in the Scriptures, from which
this place takes its name.{1a}Many people mistake Purgatory for one
of the hells,{1a}but the Purgatory of the Scriptures lies
between the Celestial Realm and Hell, a
place where the souls of the dead are
purified of sin by fire before entering{1a}the Celestial Realm.{1a}Under the present doctrine of the
Anoian faith, those with strong faith in
God go to the Celestial Realm,{1a}while those who have committed mortal
sin, and those without faith in God, are
cast down into Hell.{1a}Those who hold faith, but faith that
falls short, or who bear the stain of
lesser sins, do not enter Hell, but neither
are they permitted to enter the{1a}Celestial Realm.{1a}Such souls are cleansed of the stain of
sin through the agony of burning in the
flames of Purgatory, and are then
permitted to enter the Celestial Realm.{1a}A midpoint between the Celestial Realm
and Hell, a place where sin is purified...
Put simply, I suppose that is what it is.{1a}A soul that falls into Hell can never leave
it, but one can leave Purgatory... I would
say that is the greatest difference.{0c:02f701}

Put simply, I suppose that is what it is. // A soul that falls into Hell can never leave it, but one can leave Purgatory... I would say that is the greatest difference.

strings.jp:
{1c:10}聖書に出てくる『シェオルの柱』は、
『世界を支える柱』との意味を
持っています。{1a}天界と地獄の間にある
煉獄という世界は、何万本もの
柱によって支えられている、{1a}そしてその柱は、天界に行く直前の
霊魂によって出来ている・・・
そう聖書には書かれています。{1a}ただし、今回の場合、
本当に魂があの柱に
封じ込められているのか、
実は私にも分かりません。{1a}『眠り』でも『死』でもない・・・
そういった、
私達の理解を超えた状態を、{1a}聖書の言葉を借りて
『魂が封じ込められた』と
表現しているに過ぎないからです。{1a}ですが、
『シェオルの柱』を壊した事によって
{10}さんを含めた3人の方が
目覚めたのも事実です。{1a}{10}さん、お願いします、
『シェオルの柱』を見つけて下さい。{0c:02f601}

strings.en:
{1c:10}The 'Pillar of Sheol' in the Scriptures
carries the meaning of 'a pillar that
supports the world'.{1a}The world called Purgatory, lying
between the Celestial Realm and Hell, is
held up by tens of thousands of pillars,{1a}and those pillars are made of souls on
the very verge of going to the Celestial
Realm... So the Scriptures say.{1a}However, in this case, I do not actually
know myself whether souls are truly
sealed in those pillars.{1a}Neither 'sleep' nor 'death'... For a state
like that, beyond our understanding,{1a}we are only borrowing the words of the
Scriptures when we say 'the souls have
been sealed away'.{1a}But it is also true that breaking a 'Pillar
of Sheol' woke three people, you among
them, {10}-san.{1a}{10}-san, I beg you, please find
the 'Pillar of Sheol'.{0c:02f601}

So the Scriptures say. // However, in this case, I do not actually know myself whether souls are truly sealed in those pillars. // Neither 'sleep' nor 'death'... For a state like that, beyond our understanding, // we are only borrowing the words of the Scriptures when we say 'the souls have been sealed away'. // But it is also true that breaking a 'Pillar of Sheol' woke three people, you among them, [HERO]-san. // [HERO]-san, I beg you, please find the 'Pillar of Sheol'.

strings.jp:
{1c:10}太陽の至高神ゼメンは肉体を、
月の至高神ゼウェアクは精神を
司ると言われています。{1a}これらの調和した状態こそが
人間のあるべき姿であり、{1a}完全に調和した状態こそが、
永遠なる神の国『新しい世界』に
他ならない・・・
そう聖書には書かれています。{1a}そして、肉体のみの永遠を求め
魂を失った民は
まるで獣のごとく暴れ回り、{1a}魂のみの永遠を求め
肉体を失った民は
永遠の闇に苦しんだ・・・
こうも書かれています。{1a}あの剣が本当に
人の魂を奪うものならば、
{10}さん達こそが
最大の被害者なのでしょう。{1a}{10}さん達には
何の落ち度もないのですから。{0c:02f501}

strings.en:
{1c:10}Zemen, Supreme God of the sun, is said
to govern the body, and Zeweak,
Supreme God of the moon, the spirit.{1a}A state of harmony between these is
how humanity is meant to be,{1a}and the state of perfect harmony is
none other than the eternal kingdom of
God, the 'New World'... So the Scriptures
say.{1a}And the people who sought eternity of
the flesh alone and lost their souls ran
wild like beasts,{1a}while the people who sought eternity of
the soul alone and lost their bodies
suffered in eternal darkness... This too
is written.{1a}If that sword truly steals people's souls,
then you and the others,
{10}-san, must be its greatest
victims.{1a}For you and the others, {10}-san,
are in no way at fault.{0c:02f501}

So the Scriptures say. // And the people who sought eternity of the flesh alone and lost their souls ran wild like beasts, // while the people who sought eternity of the soul alone and lost their bodies suffered in eternal darkness... This too is written. // If that sword truly steals people's souls, then you and the others, [HERO]-san, must be its greatest victims. // For you and the others, [HERO]-san, are in no way at fault.
